alert.$description: Persistent, inline status message — the counterpart to Toast, and deliberately a separate component rather than a Toast variant. Toast is transient, floats in the top layer over arbitrary page content, and therefore MUST stay on a neutral surface (white + hairline + shadow) with only its icon carrying meaning; an Alert sits in the document flow, owns a known slot, and doesn't have to stay neutral — so it takes the role's own pale tint, which is exactly what bg.*'s $description reserved it for ('banners, badges'). Built 2026-09-07 for the Explore Degrees wizard, which needs six of them: the AI transcript reader's error and success, the 'read as a transcript from X' note, the results summary, and the 'we couldn't check your credits online' fallback. Four roles (info / success / warning / danger) — one more than Toast, which has no info because a neutral transient toast for neutral news is just noise. Anatomy is a lead + body in one paragraph (the driving copy reads '**9 classes applied to your plan.** 4 more need a quick advisor review.'), an optional quieter detail line under it, and an optional action slot for a real Button. Deferred, not forgotten: a dismissible (×) variant, and a solid/high-contrast fill for the rare blocking case — the tint covers everything the wizard needs.

gap.$description: Between the icon column and the text column.

stackGap.$description: Between the message paragraph, the detail line and the action slot.

title.$description: The lead clause. Runs INLINE with the body — one paragraph, not a heading above a block — so a screen reader reads it as one sentence and the alert stays one line tall when the copy is short.

detail.$description: The optional quieter line under the message — e.g. 'Applied to: HISTORY 120, PSYCH 120, …'. Smaller and secondary so a long enumeration doesn't compete with the message.

role.$description: Each role is a pale bg.* tint + its matching pale border.* hairline + a saturated icon. Text stays text.default at every role, never the role colour: coloured body text on a coloured tint is the 'two colour languages at once' mistake border.primary + fill.neutral already taught us, and it hurts readability for the longer copy these carry. border.* at 200 is the correct pale tint here (see that group's own note about not swapping it for fill.*) — the icon is what carries saturation.
